title: Accessibility Basics - Bosch Digital Design System
purpose: Structure accessibility principles, standards, and Bosch-specific guidelines into an AI-readable format for design, UX, and compliance workflows.

overview.mission: Enable barrier-free access to digital products for all users regardless of abilities or context.
overview.value_proposition: Accessibility improves usability for everyone and reinforces Bosch’s quality promise.

definition.accessibility: Designing digital content so all users can perceive, understand, navigate, and interact equally.
definition.design_principle: Not separate solutions, but universally usable systems across devices and conditions.

interpretation.Perceivable: Content must be visible or audible to users with different sensory abilities.
interpretation.Operable: Interfaces must be usable via different input methods (keyboard, voice, touch).
interpretation.Understandable: Content and interactions must be clear and predictable.
interpretation.Robust: Content must work across devices, browsers, and assistive technologies.

frontend_kit.requirement: ARIA labels must be filled with semantic descriptions

design_constraints.color_usage: Predefined color schemes must not be altered

inclusive_design_model.goal: Design for the widest possible range of users and contexts

interaction: Ensure clickable/touch targets are large enough
semantic: Use ARIA roles and labels correctly

governance.responsibility: Each project owner ensures compliance with local laws

key_messages: Accessibility is a universal usability requirement, not a niche feature
Design must consider situational, temporary, and permanent limitations
Compliance is legally required and enforced
Bosch provides accessible foundations, but correct implementation is critical
